title: Design: the switch-location dialog for a part sale looks as described
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an open part sale invoice {Invoice-A} made at {Location-B}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-40 Dialog.
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom, with {Customer-A} ticked and its rows showing.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click {Invoice-A}'s number.
  2. Read the dialog's title, message and buttons, letter for letter, in order.
  3. Compare the dialog with the one a work order link from another location shows today.
  4. Click "Cancel".
  5. Switch ShopView to dark theme.
  6. Click {Invoice-A}'s number again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a dialog opens over the report.
  • Step 2: title "Switch location?", message "This part sale is in " then {Location-B}'s name and "Switch your active location to view it?", then the buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel".
  • Step 3: it is the existing location-switch prompt: same look, buttons and position.
  • Step 4: the dialog closes.
  • Step 5: the page switches to dark theme.
  • Step 6: the dialog opens again and is readable in dark theme.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can)

  • S7-R3: “An invoice or part sale at another location the user is enrolled in shows the existing location-switch prompt on the report, before leaving it: title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" (for a part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?"), buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Click a part sale at another enrolled location | "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" | Same dialog”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 5 "Document links and Switch location" (board Links.dc.html). The design draws the work order version of the dialog only; the part sale message is not pictured.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p5-another-location-asks-first.png: figure "Another location asks first" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)"

The design's own words:

  • ""Switch location? This work order is in Staging Lethbridge - 4310. Switch your active location to view it?" on the report. Switch Location opens it there. S7-R3, S7-R4." (caption of "Another location asks first")

Difference from the PRD (DD-01): the PRD says buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel" (S7-R3), title "Switch location?"; the design shows buttons "Cancel" (left, grey) then "Switch Location" (right, blue, capital L), and a close "×" at the top right of the dialog; caption: "Switch Location opens it there.". This case follows the PRD; the difference is question 11 on Chris Ward's question sheet (added 22 Oct 2026); the design version is held in D-76.
